items.question: Mặc định Lambda thử lại lỗi throttling và lỗi hệ thống của lời gọi bất đồng bộ trong bao lâu?
items.reference_answer: For 429 throttling and 500-series system errors, Lambda retries from its queue for up to six hours by default, with exponential intervals.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Throttle/system errors use up to six hours of default queue retries, with exponential spacing.

alternatives.quote: If the Event Function doesn't have enough concurrency available to process all events, additional requests are throttled. For throttling errors (429) and system errors (500-series), Lambda returns the event to the queue and attempts to run the function again for up to 6 hours by default. The retry interval increases exponentially from 1 second after the first attempt to a maximum of 5 minutes. If the queue contains many entries, Lambda increases the retry interval and reduces the rate at which it reads events from the queue.

items.question: Lambda có thể gửi lại event bất đồng bộ dù hàm không trả lỗi không?
items.reference_answer: Yes. Its eventually consistent queue can deliver duplicates even when the function returns no error; handlers should handle duplicate events.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Duplicate asynchronous events are possible without function errors.

alternatives.quote: Even if your Event Function doesn't return an error, it's possible for it to receive the same event from Lambda multiple times because the queue itself is eventually consistent. If the function can't keep up with incoming events, events might also be deleted from the queue without being sent to the function. Ensure that your function code gracefully handles duplicate events, and that you have enough concurrency available to handle all invocations.

items.question: Làm sao lưu event bất đồng bộ bị loại bỏ và bản ghi Lambda invocation thất bại?
items.reference_answer: A dead-letter queue captures discarded events; an on-failure destination captures records of failed invocations.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Dead-letter queues capture discarded events and on-failure destinations capture failed invocation records.

alternatives.quote: When the queue is very long, new events might age out before Lambda has a chance to send them to your Event Function. When an event expires or fails all processing attempts, Lambda discards it. You can configure error handling for an Event Function to reduce the number of retries that Lambda performs, or to discard unprocessed events more quickly. To capture discarded events, configure a dead-letter queue for the function. To capture records of failed invocations (such as timeouts or runtime errors), create an on-failure destination.

items.question: Lambda do S3 kích hoạt tránh tự gọi lặp khi ghi kết quả ra sao?

alternatives.quote: If your Lambda Event Function uses the same bucket that triggers it, it could cause the function to run in a loop. For example, if the bucket triggers a function each time an object is uploaded, and the function uploads an object to the bucket, then the function indirectly triggers itself. To avoid this, use two buckets, or configure the trigger to only apply to a prefix used for incoming objects.

items.question: Trong phép so allow/deny cùng tài khoản được tài liệu IAM mô tả, identity policy và resource policy kết hợp thế nào?
items.reference_answer: The documented same-account comparison takes the union of allows, with an explicit deny overriding an allow; other applicable policy types may add constraints.

evidence_groups.required_fact: The documented same-account identity/resource comparison combines allows by union, subject to explicit deny.

alternatives.quote: Identity-based policies and resource-based policies grant permissions to the identities or resources to which they are attached. When an IAM entity (user or role) requests access to a resource within the same account, AWS evaluates all the permissions granted by the identity-based and resource-based policies. The resulting permissions are the union of the permissions of the two types. If an action is allowed by an identity-based policy, a resource-based policy, or both, then AWS allows the action. An explicit deny in either of these policies overrides the allow.

items.question: Identity policy cho phép có vượt được permissions boundary không cho hành động đó không?
items.reference_answer: No. Effective permissions are the intersection of identity policies and the permissions boundary; explicit deny overrides allow.

evidence_groups.required_fact: A permissions boundary constrains identity-based permissions by intersection.

alternatives.quote: When AWS evaluates the identity-based policies and permissions boundary for a user, the resulting permissions are the intersection of the two categories. That means that when you add a permissions boundary to a user with existing identity-based policies, you might reduce the actions that the user can perform. Alternatively, when you remove a permissions boundary from a user, you might increase the actions they can perform. An explicit deny in either of these policies overrides the allow. To view information about how other policy types are evaluated with permissions boundaries, see Evaluating effective permissions with boundaries.
